messages:
danielle: Quick arch follow-up: notes from today on operator-scope issuance and runtime gatekeeping. Wanted to capture decisions and open questions.

simon: missed it, short TL;DR?

danielle: Root problem: teams mint wide keys 'because convenience'. We want a safe pattern that preserves low-latency fanout but prevents operator keys from being de facto admins.

maya: Two new concepts we floated that I think are worth capturing: (1) attestation badges on tokens (signed assertion from infra) and (2) paired ephemeral per-project tokens derived from a single operator handle.

lina: Explain the paired token idea real quick?

maya: Operator mint returns a short-lived opaque handle (H). Worker uses H + mTLS to call token-exchange service to get per-project token T_p for project P. T_p is short TTL and scoped narrowly. H is usable only from allowed infra e.g., svc-scheduler and has attestation claim. This lets us avoid sending a single wide token everywhere while keeping latency by caching T_p locally.

jordan: I like that. We should require an approval_id and store a proof-of-intent record when H is minted. Approval_id surfaces in audits.

danielle: Decisions captured so far:
- Minting: default = project-scoped tokens. Operator-scope mint (returns handle H) requires approval_id and an attestation badge from the caller identity (issuer_type=system + signed attestor).
- Token shape: H has claims: issuer=svc, env=[infra|scheduler], attest=true, billing_tag. T_p includes project claim and explicit resource verbs.
- TTL: H max 6h; T_p max 30m; cache T_p in node-local KV for reuse.

simon: How does runtime routing pick operator pool vs project pool?

danielle: Routing rules: if request presents H and H.attest==true and H.env in (infra,scheduler) -> allow exchange for T_p and route using T_p. If request presents full-token with cross-project scope -> reject unless migration whitelist. Deny-by-default otherwise.

lina: Migration plan? We can't rotate keys overnight.

jordan: Phases:
1) Discovery (2 weeks): collect existing wide keys, tag owners, instrument last-used project graph and billing footprint.
2) Badge rollout (3 weeks): enable attestation attestors and minting path for H; log-only enforcement for exchange endpoints.
3) Soft-enforce (2 weeks): reject non-attested operator tokens to operator-only endpoints; continue logging.
4) Enforce (ongoing): require approval_id for new H mints, sunset legacy wide keys after N days.

maya: Metrics to watch during each phase: rate of rejected calls, percent of fanout jobs using cached T_p, median added tail latency for fanout, and auditing gaps (unowned keys).

simon: What about cross-org?

danielle: Cross-org requires explicit cross-org grant with approval and must set cross_org=true claim; routing will only allow it for specific endpoints and shorter TTL (e.g., H cross-org max 1h, T_p 10m).

lina: UI/Console changes: credential listing must show handle H entries distinct from raw keys with an "attested operator" badge, approval_id link, last seen projects mini-heatmap, and a revoke button that triggers pre-warm fallback tests.

jordan: Failover playbook highlights:
- If operator-exchange service is unhealthy, routing layer tries per-target project-service key exchange using service's project-local mint endpoints, rate-limited and backoff applied.
- Pre-warm: job launcher can pre-warm T_p for top-K targets to reduce tail latency.
- Emergency revoke: revoke H and start graceful fallback mode where scheduler uses per-project tokens for 1 hour while ops triage.

maya: Perf note: implement microbenchmarks for exchange-cached path vs single operator direct call. If cached exchange median overhead >20ms per-target we need to mandate batching in consumers.

danielle: Security guardrails:
- approve gating: require 2 approvers for teams to request persistent H mint rights.
- enforcement: deny-by-default on any endpoint not explicitly mapped to operator exchange.
- audit: every H mint must record approval_id, actor, and a comment; surface in logs and Console.

simon: Implementation tasks called out:
- simon: middleware that validates attestation badge and instruments mismatches (EOW).
- jordan: draft IAM role templates for operator handles + approval workflow and a sample policy set (next Tue).
- lina: Console mocks for handle listing, approval flow, and heatmap (next Thu).
- maya: perf experiment plan + microbench harness for cached exchange and pre-warm (2 weeks).

danielle: Open questions we still need in RFC: exact claim names and enum values (avoid ambiguous strings), attestor trust model (signing keys & rotation), and the expiration windows for H and T_p. I'll enumerate options in the RFC.

jordan: Also add a quick incident test: simulate operator pool outage and run the fallback path in staging to validate fallback latency and concurrency limits.

lina: I can take the Console mock task unless someone else wants it.

simon: lgtm

ops-bot: Reminder: planned migration windows will generate monitoring alerts; coordinate with oncall and update runbook.

danielle: Great. I'll draft the RFC (will include precise claim names, handle/token formats, migration phases, rollback playbook, and the approval UX). Posting link when ready. Thanks all.
